clue.text: I'm telling you definitely, it's a puncture!

explanation.surface: A motorist exclaims with certainty on discovering a burst tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of closing an argument, and it also literally describes a deflated tyre.

clue.text: End of part of school year in America

parts.note: a term is one of the divisions of the school year
taken as written
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone asks when part of the school year ends in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final stop or end point of a route or line.

clue.text: Cartoonist removed from main rota

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved about into a new order, as if shifted around

explanation.surface: A cartoon artist has been taken off the main duty roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as taken off the rota, but here it signals re-moving the letters of MAIN ROTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator draws the frames of cartoons, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Dummy shoot

explanation.surface: Two terse words, a fool and a sprouting stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy is a gullible person, a dupe; a sucker is also a shoot springing from a plant's roots or stem.

clue.text: Only a little of similar value like a caterpillar

indicators.note: Only a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something is said to be only slightly of comparable worth to a caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth, so caterpillar-like means in the larva stage.

clue.text: Our Tom is dreadfully fearful

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a bad way, so these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Our cat Tom is terribly scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous is a synonym of frightened or timid.

clue.text: Boy returns after exercises with one part of a bicycle

indicators.note: after puts the reversed boy following the exercises in the answer

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise

indicators.note: returns means the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy comes back from PE with a piece of his bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is the foot lever that turns a bicycle's crank.

clue.text: Returning at intervals to this chemical table

explanation.surface: Something recurs regularly in relation to a table of the chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring at regular intervals is the everyday sense; Mendeleev's arrangement of the elements is the Periodic Table.

clue.text: One not accepting that it's a measure of the fineness of silk

definitions.text: a measure of the fineness of silk

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept that this is how silk thread is graded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to admit something is a denier; a denier is also a unit of thread weight used for silk and hosiery.

clue.text: Bedding for new-born animals?

explanation.surface: A question about straw put down for young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw strewn for livestock to lie on is litter, and a brood of young born together is also a litter.

clue.text: Scoff at leading vehicle carriage

indicators.note: leading puts the scoffing word in front of the vehicle

parts.note: to rail at is to scoff at or berate
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the front car of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled railway carriage.

clue.text: One scraping a living?

parts.note: scraping a living usually means barely getting by, but here it is someone who earns money by scraping a bow across strings

explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle player draws the bow across the strings, so a professional one literally earns by scraping.

clue.text: Such history is only to be expected?

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain kind of history is predictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history is the study of plants and animals, and natural also means normal or to be expected.

clue.text: Commander?

parts.note: not a naval rank here but simply someone who gives commands or instructions

explanation.definitionFit: One who orders is literally one who commands.

clue.text: Outstanding achievement of out-of-work trade unionists?

definitions.text: Outstanding achievement of out-of-work trade unionists?

parts.words: Outstanding achievement of out-of-work trade unionists?
parts.note: a triumph read as one won by workers who have walked out in industrial action

explanation.definitionFit: A remarkable triumph is a smash hit, and workers on strike who win would literally have such a result.

clue.text: Regal nipper?

parts.note: a nipper is a child, but here it is a royal-sounding creature that pinches with claws

explanation.definitionFit: This large crustacean has a royal title in its name and claws that nip.

clue.text: Roving salesmen are anonymous

indicators.note: roving means wandering about, so the letters of salesmen wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen go unnamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no known name is anonymous.

clue.text: Pal close to removing shellfish

indicators.note: read as re-moving, so the letters of the two words are moved again into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend near to taking away seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' is read as re-moving, rearranging the letters of PAL CLOSE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop is a variant name for the scallop, a bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Show indifference when it's cold

parts.note: giving the cold version of a body part is an idiom for snubbing someone

explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to ignore or rebuff them.

clue.text: Initially such a word is formed

definitions.text: Initially such a word is formed

parts.words: Initially such a word is formed
parts.note: a word made from the first letters, or initials, of other words

explanation.definitionFit: A word like NATO or radar is built from the initial letters of a phrase.

clue.text: A cab with a lack of coordination

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

explanation.surface: A taxi ride leaves someone unsteady on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is the medical term for loss of control of bodily movements.

clue.text: Troublesome money!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Troublesome money!' (6): the currency is hidden in 'Troublesome', whose own '-some' is the only hint that letters are taken out, so one word is both fodder and indicator; no source gives a separate indicator word.

clue.text: Joseph pointedly wealthy in the old city

parts.note: J is an abbreviation of the name Joseph
E, east, is a point of the compass
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: Joseph, clearly rich, lived in the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointedly' gives a compass point, E; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is an ancient city of the West Bank, famed for its fallen walls.

clue.text: Jack produced discordant groan in pidgin

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: discordant means out of harmony, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Jack let out a harsh groan in a mixed trade language.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon once meant a hybrid language or pidgin, as well as specialist speech.

clue.text: Get back, are lacking a successful move

indicators.note: lacking means the word are is without the following letter

parts.note: a coup is a sudden successful stroke or move

explanation.surface: Someone recovers, though missing a winning strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money or losses.

clue.text: Descriptive of a pawnbroker, relatively speaking?

definitions.text: Descriptive of a pawnbroker, relatively speaking?

parts.words: Descriptive of a pawnbroker, relatively speaking?
parts.note: a pawnbroker is jocularly called uncle, and relatively points to family relations

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so an uncle-like adjective fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means like or relating to an uncle, and 'uncle' is slang for a pawnbroker.

clue.text: Made a low guttural sound develop that had taken precedence

parts.note: to grow is to develop
led means went first, took precedence

explanation.surface: Someone describes a noise coming about after taking the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that snarls deep in the throat is said to have growled.

clue.text: Toss the caber with bitter result

indicators.note: to toss something is to throw it about, so the letters of caber land in a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland games athlete throws the pole and feels sour about the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland games event in which a long pole is flipped end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare synonym of sour or harsh.

clue.text: It is used for polishing grains before father gets through

indicators.note: before puts the grains ahead of what follows

parts.note: sand is made of fine grains
pa is a familiar word for father
per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: Grains go first, and then father makes it through.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is rubbed on wood to smooth and polish it.
